verdict.reasoning: Independently confirmed against both rendered PDF pages and the raw markdown bytes; no part of the claim is a misquote, and the defect is not page-break furniture, wrapping, or hyphenation. PDF evidence (scripts/spec/page_workunit.py, 300 dpi): - E:/Temp/specrecon/v163/spec_p163.png (printed folio 133) ends with 8.4.3.4.4 General rules, item 1) '…applicable form of INVOKE statement, as follows:' followed by an indented two-line block, each form on its own line: INVOKE identifier-1 literal-1 USING arguments RETURNING temp-identifier INVOKE identifier-1 literal-1 RETURNING temp-identifier - E:/Temp/specrecon/v164/spec_p164.png (printed folio 134) opens with the continuation of that same indented block, again one form per line: INVOKE object-class-name-1 literal-1 USING arguments RETURNING temp-identifier INVOKE object-class-name-1 literal-1 RETURNING temp-identifier then a blank line, then the flush lead-in 'where:', then a) / b) / c). So the printed list is unambiguously FOUR distinct INVOKE substitution forms, set one per line, with 'where:' as a separate lead-in paragraph — exactly as claimed. Markdown evidence (exact bytes, awk NR 7075-7080): 7075|[1) An inline method invocation references a temporary data item … as follows:] 7076|[] 7077|[ INVOKE identifier-1 literal-1 USING arguments RETURNING temp-identifier] 7078|[ INVOKE identifier-1 literal-1 RETURNING temp-identifier INVOKE object-class-name-1 literal-1 USING arguments RETURNING temp-identifier INVOKE object-class-name-1 literal-1 RETURNING temp-identifier where:] 7079|[] 7080|[] Line 7078 matches the claimed quote character-for-character. Forms 2, 3 and 4 plus the 'where:' lead-in are run together on one physical line, and all of it sits before the page-164 anchor. Why this is not a formatting-only difference: the block is NOT inside a code fence and is indented only three spaces, so it is not an indented code block either. Under CommonMark, lines 7077 and 7078 are consecutive non-blank lines of the same paragraph, so a renderer joins them too — all four forms and 'where:' collapse into one continuous run-on sentence with no separators. Nothing in the text marks where one form ends and the next begins, so the enumeration itself is destroyed, not merely re-wrapped. That enumeration is load-bearing normative content: 8.4.3.4.3 syntax rule 3 (page 163) reads 'One of the INVOKE statements specified in General rule 1 shall be valid according to 14.9.23', which is only meaningful if the four alternatives are distinguishable. A reader/tool consuming the markdown cannot determine that object-class-name-1 forms exist as separate alternatives, nor that 'where:' introduces a) b) c) rather than being a token of an INVOKE statement. A grep for 'INVOKE object-class-name-1 literal-1' across the whole spec returns line 7078 only, so the correct per-line rendering exists nowhere else in the file — the content is not recoverable elsewhere. Page-attribution half of the claim also holds: the two object-class-name-1 forms and the 'where:' lead-in are printed at the top of PDF page 164 but are filed inside the page-163 slice (before the line-7080 anchor), and E:/Temp/specrecon/v164/page-164.md begins directly at 'a) arguments are the operands specified within parentheses…'. A page-anchored citation to the object-class-name-1 forms therefore resolves to page 163.
verdict.corrected_description: Confirmed, with one detail worse than described. Under 8.4.3.4.4 General rule 1, the ISO standard prints a four-line list of INVOKE substitution forms, one form per line: the two identifier-1 forms at the foot of page 163 (printed folio 133) and the two object-class-name-1 forms at the top of page 164 (printed folio 134), followed by a blank line and the separate lead-in 'where:'. In specs/ISO_COBOL.md the second, third and fourth forms plus 'where:' are concatenated onto a single physical line (line 7078), and — because the block is neither fenced nor indented four spaces — line 7077 (the first form) is part of the same markdown paragraph, so on render ALL FOUR forms and the 'where:' lead-in collapse into one unbroken run-on with no delimiters. The distinct-alternatives structure that syntax rule 3 ('One of the INVOKE statements specified in General rule 1 shall be valid') depends on is therefore unrecoverable from the transcription. Separately, the page-164 material (both object-class-name-1 forms and 'where:') is filed before the `` anchor at line 7080, so it is attributed to page 163. Fix: restore the four forms as four separate lines inside a fenced block, keep 'where:' as its own paragraph, and move the last two forms plus 'where:' after the page-164 anchor.
